segments.text: # CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
# 1 Using this guide
This guide explains the error codes that the CP-200 controller shows and the mechanical problems it can't detect.
Each code's section says what the code means, when the controller raises it, the likely causes in the order to check them and how to clear it.
Codes starting with E-1 concern the motor and its supply, E-2 the hydraulics and the seal, and E-3 the controller and its sensors.
Work through the causes in order.
If you clear a code and it returns within an hour, stop and raise a work order instead of resetting it again.

Error E-222 means the vibration on the bearing housing exceeded 7.1 mm/s RMS.
The controller warns at 4.5 mm/s RMS and trips the pump at 7.1 mm/s RMS.
Causes, most likely first:

Don't restart the pump repeatedly after E-222.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-106: supply undervoltage

segments.text: ## Error E-106: supply undervoltage
Error E-106 means the supply voltage stayed below 90 percent of its nominal value for more than 5 seconds.
The pump restarts by itself 30 seconds after the voltage returns, unless automatic restart is disabled.
Causes, most likely first:
1. A weak supply during the start of another large motor.
2. A failing transformer tap changer.
E-106 clears itself.
If it repeats, record the times and ask the plant electrical engineer to check the supply.

evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text: # SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.
1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C.
Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027.
From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.
The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged.
Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy.
Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.

Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started.
They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.
Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.

evidence.section: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

segments.text: # Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.
Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing.
Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open.
Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.

segments.text: # 5 Operation
Run a new gearbox at no more than half load for its first 50 hours.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

segments.text: ## Error E-104: motor winding temperature high
Error E-104 means the motor's winding temperature exceeded 155 °C.
The controller trips the pump and blocks a restart until the windings cool below 120 °C.
Check the motor's cooling fan and fan cover for blockages, and measure the supply voltage on all three phases; an unbalance of more than 2 percent overheats the windings.
Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.
Reset E-104 at the local panel once the temperature has dropped.
Never bypass the thermistor relay.

segments.text: # SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.

6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-102: supply phase missing

segments.text: ## Error E-102: supply phase missing
Error E-102 means one of the three supply phases is missing.
1. A blown fuse in the motor feeder.
2. A loose terminal in the motor control center.
E-102 clears itself when all three phases return.
## Error E-103: wrong phase sequence
Error E-103 means the supply phase sequence is reversed, so the pump would run backwards.
The controller blocks the start; it never trips a running pump for E-103.
## Error E-104: motor winding temperature high
Error E-104 means the motor's winding temperature exceeded 155 °C.
Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.
Reset E-104 at the local panel once the temperature has dropped.

segments.text: ## Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

Check the motor's cooling fan and fan cover for blockages, and measure the supply voltage on all three phases; an unbalance of more than 2 percent overheats the windings.
Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.
Never bypass the thermistor relay.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start

segments.text: # 5 Commissioning
## 5.1 Checks before the first start
1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
## 5.4 Start-up
Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.
1. Open the suction valve fully.
Never throttle the suction side.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection.
The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes.
During the first hour, check that the bearing temperatures stay below 80 °C and listen for cavitation noise.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Seal leakage

segments.text: ## Seal leakage
A new mechanical seal may drip for the first few hours while its faces run in.
A seal that leaks steadily after that has worn or damaged faces.
The most common causes are dry running, seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar and abrasive particles in the seal water.
Replace the seal as SOP-FS-014 describes; don't try to stop a leak by tightening the gland nuts beyond their torque.

segments.text: # SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026.
This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.
1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires.

Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.

5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

| F016 | Cooling fan failure | Fan blocked or worn out | Replace fan PN-7716-A |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
## Fault F012: output overcurrent
Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating.
The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.
A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds.
Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.
Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V.
It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load.
Fault F010 means the speed reference on a 4 to 20 mA input fell below 2 mA, which the drive reads as a broken wire.
The drive stops the motor rather than run at an unknown speed.

segments.text: # 4 Lubrication
## 4.1 Lubrication
The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil.
Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first.
Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.
Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped.
In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.
## 4.2 Approved oils
Table 4-1 Approved oils
| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
Don't mix mineral and synthetic oils.
When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text: ## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low
Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low.
The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal.
Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.
1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
2. A blocked strainer upstream of V-114 (work instruction WI-FS-031 describes the cleaning).
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31.
To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel.
If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Seal leakage

segments.text: ## Seal leakage
A new mechanical seal may drip for the first few hours while its faces run in.
A seal that leaks steadily after that has worn or damaged faces.
The most common causes are dry running, seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar and abrasive particles in the seal water.
Replace the seal as SOP-FS-014 describes; don't try to stop a leak by tightening the gland nuts beyond their torque.

segments.text: # Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.
Verify zero energy before work starts.
Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open.
Each person working on the pump fits their own lock.
This bulletin applies to every pump with a mechanical seal flushed by seal water, not only to the CP-200.
Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.
At the Riverside plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Riverside maintenance planner on extension 4410 before work starts.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start

segments.text: # 5 Commissioning
## 5.1 Checks before the first start
1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
4. Flush the suction pipe and the seal-water line before connecting them.
## 5.4 Start-up
Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.
1. Open the suction valve fully.
Never throttle the suction side.
2. Vent the casing at the vent plug until water flows without air.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection.
The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes.
Running against a closed discharge valve for longer overheats the liquid in the casing.
During the first hour, check that the bearing temperatures stay below 80 °C and listen for cavitation noise.

segments.text: ## 6.3 Flange bolt torque
Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts.
The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.
| Bolt size | Torque |
Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m.
Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m.
Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.
Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets.
A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.
## 6.4 Seal housing bolts
Tighten the four seal housing bolts to 45 N·m.
Fit the seal housing before the bearing housing is bolted back to the casing, so that the seal can be centered on the shaft.

evidence.title: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
evidence.section: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

segments.text: # WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description

segments.text: # 2 Description
The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C.
The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.
A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

| Item | Value |
| Flow range | 40 to 240 m³/h |

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text: ## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low
Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low.
The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal.
Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.
1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel.
If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 9 Troubleshooting

segments.text: # 9 Troubleshooting
The controller shows an error code for most faults; the CP-200 troubleshooting guide explains each code.
Table 9-1 lists faults that the controller can't detect.
Table 9-1 Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |
| Pump doesn't deliver | Suction valve closed or casing not vented | Open the suction valve fully and vent the casing |
| Delivery falls off over weeks | Worn wear ring or impeller | Check the impeller clearance (section 6.2) |
| Seal leaks steadily | Worn seal faces | Replace the mechanical seal (section 8.1) |
| Motor overloads | Pump runs far right of its curve | Throttle the discharge valve to the duty point |

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-310: communication lost

segments.text: ## Error E-310: communication lost
Error E-310 means the controller hasn't heard from the plant control system for 30 seconds.
The pump keeps running at its last set point.
Causes, most likely first:
1. A network fault.
2. The plant control system was restarted.
E-310 clears itself when communication returns.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-105: earth fault

segments.text: ## Error E-105: earth fault
Error E-105 means the controller measured a leakage current to earth above 300 mA.
The earth-fault relay trips the pump at once.
Causes, most likely first:
1. Water in the motor terminal box.
2. Damaged motor cable insulation.
Don't reset E-105 until an electrician has measured the motor's insulation resistance.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-204: flow low

segments.text: ## Error E-204: flow low
Error E-204 means the flow fell below 40 m³/h, the pump's minimum continuous flow.
The controller warns at once and trips the pump after 2 minutes of low flow.
Causes, most likely first:
1. The discharge valve is throttled too far.
2. The process no longer needs the pump.
Open the discharge valve or stop the pump, then reset E-204.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-221: bearing temperature high

segments.text: ## Error E-221: bearing temperature high
Error E-221 means a bearing temperature exceeded 95 °C.
The controller warns at 85 °C and trips the pump at 95 °C.
Causes, most likely first:
1. Too much grease after regreasing.
2. Misalignment between pump and motor.
3. A worn bearing.
Let the bearings cool, check the alignment and the amount of grease, then reset E-221.

segments.text: ## Error E-303: bearing temperature sensor fault
Error E-303 means one of the bearing temperature sensors TE-21 and TE-22 reports an open circuit.
The pump keeps running without bearing temperature protection on that bearing.
Causes, most likely first:
1. A loose sensor connector.
2. A failed sensor.
Reseat the connector; replace the sensor if E-303 returns.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Troubleshooting: excessive vibration

segments.text: # 3 Mechanical problems
## Troubleshooting: excessive vibration
Vibration above 4.5 mm/s RMS on the bearing housing needs investigation; above 7.1 mm/s RMS, stop the pump.
Likely causes, in the order to check them:
- Misalignment between the pump and motor shafts after maintenance.
Check the coupling alignment.
It comes from low suction pressure: check that the suction valve is fully open and the suction strainer is clean.
- Worn bearings.
Bearing noise rises before the vibration does.
- A loose baseplate or loose foot bolts.
- A damaged or unbalanced impeller.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-231: liquid temperature high

segments.text: ## Error E-231: liquid temperature high
Error E-231 means the liquid temperature in the casing exceeded 90 °C.
The controller trips the pump after 10 seconds above the limit.
Causes, most likely first:
1. The pump ran against a closed discharge valve.
2. The process supplies liquid hotter than the pump's rating.
Let the casing cool and find out why the liquid overheated before resetting E-231.

segments.text: # 2 Product description
The HG-400 is a foot-mounted helical gearbox with parallel input and output shafts.
The housing is cast iron with cooling fins on both sides.
## 2.1 Type designation
The type code on the nameplate gives the frame size, the number of stages and the nominal ratio.
For example, HG-400-2-12.5 is a two-stage gearbox with a ratio of 12.5 to 1.
Table 2-1 Ratings at 1,500 rpm input
| Ratio | Stages | Output torque | Thermal rating |
The thermal rating is the power the gearbox can transmit continuously without the oil exceeding 90 °C at an ambient temperature of 25 °C.
Above 35 °C ambient, derate it by 10 percent for every 5 °C.

evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 3 Installation › 3.2 Mounting

segments.text: ## 3.2 Mounting
Mount the HG-400 on a flat, rigid base; the mounting surface must be flat to within 0.1 mm.
Put shims under the feet, never under the gearbox housing.
## 3.3 Shaft connections
Fit couplings and sprockets by heating them to about 100 °C; never hammer them onto the shafts, because the impact damages the bearings.
Keep the overhung load on the output shaft within the value on the nameplate.

evidence.title: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual
evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 4 Lubrication › 4.1 Lubrication

segments.text: The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil.
Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first.
Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.
Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped.
In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.
## 4.2 Approved oils
Table 4-1 Approved oils
| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
Don't mix mineral and synthetic oils.
When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

This procedure applies the oil change in section 4.3 of the HG-400 manual at Contoso plants and adds the checks that the plants' oil analysis program needs.
2. Take an oil sample from the middle of the sight glass level before draining, and label it with the gearbox tag.

segments.text: # 7 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |
| Whining noise that rises with speed | Low oil level or worn gear teeth | Top up the oil; inspect the gears if the noise stays |
| Knocking noise once per revolution | Damaged gear tooth | Stop the gearbox and inspect the gears |
| Oil leaks at a shaft | Worn shaft seal or blocked breather | Clean the breather; replace the seal |
| Oil temperature above 90 °C | Overload, wrong oil or dirty cooling fins | Check the load and the oil; clean the fins |

segments.text: ## Fault F012: output overcurrent
Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating.
The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.
A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds.
Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.
## Fault F002: DC bus overvoltage
Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V.
It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load.
Raise parameter 2-11 (ramp-down time), or fit a brake resistor if the process needs fast stops.

segments.text: # 4 Faults
A fault stops the motor and shows its code on the display.
Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F002 | DC bus overvoltage | Ramp-down time too short for the load's inertia | Raise parameter 2-11 or fit a brake resistor |
| F003 | Heatsink overtemperature | Blocked air flow or a failed fan | Clean the air path; check the fan (F016) |
| F004 | Earth fault | Damaged motor cable or wet motor | Measure the insulation before resetting |
| F005 | Motor overload (I²t) | Motor current above its rating for too long | Check the load; check parameter 1-03 |
| F006 | Input phase loss | A blown supply fuse | Replace the fuse and find out why it blew |
| F007 | Motor phase loss | Loose motor cable terminal | Tighten the motor terminals |
| F008 | Fieldbus timeout | No message from the controller for 2 seconds | Check the network cable and the controller |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F015 | Parameter memory error | Corrupt parameters after a power cut during a save | Restore the parameter backup |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
| F021 | Underload | Motor current below 15 percent while running | Check for a broken belt or coupling |

## Fault F010: analog input lost

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-221: bearing temperature high

segments.text: ## Error E-221: bearing temperature high
Error E-221 means a bearing temperature exceeded 95 °C.
Causes, most likely first:
1. Too much grease after regreasing.
2. Misalignment between pump and motor.
3. A worn bearing.
## Error E-222: vibration high
Error E-222 means the vibration on the bearing housing exceeded 7.1 mm/s RMS.
The controller warns at 4.5 mm/s RMS and trips the pump at 7.1 mm/s RMS.
Causes, most likely first:
1. Misalignment after maintenance.
2. Cavitation.
3. Worn bearings or a damaged impeller.
Section 3.1 describes how to find the cause.

evidence.section: Engineering change notice ECN-2291: CP-200 mechanical seal › Engineering change notice ECN-2291

segments.text: # Engineering change notice ECN-2291
| Change notice | ECN-2291 |
Effective September 14, 2026, mechanical seal PN-4471-B is superseded by PN-4471-C on all CP-200 pumps.
PN-4471-C has a silicon-carbide face rated for higher seal-water temperatures.
Fit PN-4471-C at the next seal replacement and quarantine remaining PN-4471-B stock.
Reason for the change: three PN-4471-B failures in 2026 were traced to wear of the carbon face at seal-water temperatures above 60 °C.
The manual will be revised in 2027; until then, this notice takes precedence over it.

segments.text: # SVC-POL-002: Response times for contracted customers
Field Services commits to these response times for customers with a service contract, measured from the time the call is logged:
| Priority | Definition | On-site response |
| P1 | Production stopped, or a safety risk | 4 hours |
| P2 | Production degraded | 1 business day |
| P3 | Planned or cosmetic work | 5 business days |
The dispatcher agrees the priority with the customer when the call is logged.
Escalate any P1 call that has no engineer assigned after 30 minutes to the Field Services duty manager.
Response times are measured from the time the call is logged to the time the engineer arrives on site.
Calls logged outside working hours count from 07:00 the next business day, except P1 calls, which count from the time they are logged.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 6 Assembly and disassembly › 6.3 Flange bolt torque

segments.text: ## 6.3 Flange bolt torque
Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts.
The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.
| Bolt size | Torque |
Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m.
Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m.
Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.
Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets.
A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.
## 6.4 Seal housing bolts
Tighten the four seal housing bolts to 45 N·m.
Fit the seal housing before the bearing housing is bolted back to the casing, so that the seal can be centered on the shaft.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start

segments.text: # 5 Commissioning
## 5.1 Checks before the first start
1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
## 5.4 Start-up
Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.
1. Open the suction valve fully.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection.
The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes.
During the first hour, check that the bearing temperatures stay below 80 °C and listen for cavitation noise.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

segments.text: Error E-104 means the motor's winding temperature exceeded 155 °C.
The controller trips the pump and blocks a restart until the windings cool below 120 °C.
Check the motor's cooling fan and fan cover for blockages, and measure the supply voltage on all three phases; an unbalance of more than 2 percent overheats the windings.
Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.
Reset E-104 at the local panel once the temperature has dropped.
Never bypass the thermistor relay.

The pump restarts by itself 30 seconds after the voltage returns, unless automatic restart is disabled.
Causes, most likely first:
1. A weak supply during the start of another large motor.
2. A failing transformer tap changer.
E-106 clears itself.
If it repeats, record the times and ask the plant electrical engineer to check the supply.

segments.text: ## Error E-203: dry running
Error E-203 means the dry-running sensor in the casing detected no liquid.
The controller trips the pump at once, because a few seconds of dry running damage the mechanical seal.
Causes, most likely first:
1. The casing wasn't vented after maintenance.
2. The suction tank ran empty.
Vent the casing until water flows without air, then reset E-203.
Check the seal for leaks after the restart.

evidence.title: SOP-FS-007: Pump isolation and lockout
evidence.section: SOP-FS-007: Pump isolation and lockout

segments.text: # SOP-FS-007: Pump isolation and lockout
Revision 5, effective May 12, 2025.
This procedure isolates a pump so that it can't start, can't be pressurized and can't move while people work on it.
It implements safety bulletin SB-0932 for Fluid Systems pumps.
## Isolation steps
1. Tell the control room which pump you are isolating and why.
2. Stop the pump from the local panel and open the motor's isolator.
3. Fit your own padlock and tag to the isolator.
Everyone who works on the pump fits their own lock.
4. Close the suction and discharge valves and lock them closed.
5. Close the seal-water isolation valve upstream of the strainer and open the blow-down valve.
6. Open the casing drain and wait until it stops flowing.
7. Try to start the pump from the local panel to prove that it can't start, then return the switch to off.
8. Check that every pressure gauge on the pump reads zero.
## Removing the isolation
Remove the isolation in the reverse order once everyone has removed their lock.
The last person to remove a lock checks that the coupling guard is fitted and that no tools are left on the skid.
## Seal-water valves at Riverside
At the Riverside plant, the seal-water valve for each pump carries the pump's tag with the prefix V: valve V-114 feeds pump P-201.
Don't close V-114 itself for isolation; close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer, so that V-114's setting is kept.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.4 Start-up

segments.text: ## 5.4 Start-up
Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.
1. Open the suction valve fully.
Never throttle the suction side.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes.

segments.text: ## 6.3 Flange bolt torque
Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts.
The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.
| Bolt size | Torque |
Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m.
Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m.
Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.
Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets.
A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.

segments.text: ## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low
Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low.
The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal.
Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.
1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31.
Compare its reading with the local gauge.
To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel.
If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 3 Installation › 3.2 Mounting

segments.text: ## 3.2 Mounting
Mount the HG-400 on a flat, rigid base; the mounting surface must be flat to within 0.1 mm.
Use the four M16 foot bolts of property class 8.8 and tighten them to 195 N·m in a cross pattern.
Put shims under the feet, never under the gearbox housing.
After mounting, align the input and output couplings as their installation instructions describe, and check that the breather plug on top of the housing is fitted and open.
## 3.3 Shaft connections
Fit couplings and sprockets by heating them to about 100 °C; never hammer them onto the shafts, because the impact damages the bearings.
Keep the overhung load on the output shaft within the value on the nameplate.

evidence.title: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual
evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 4 Lubrication › 4.3 Oil change

segments.text: ## 4.3 Oil change
1. Run the gearbox until the oil is warm, so that it drains completely, then stop and lock out the motor.
2. Remove the breather plug and the drain plug and let the oil drain into a container.
3. Clean the magnetic drain plug and note any metal particles on it in the work order.
4. Refit the drain plug with a new sealing ring and tighten it to 80 N·m.
5. Fill the gearbox through the breather opening until the oil reaches the middle of the sight glass.
6. Refit the breather plug and run the gearbox for ten minutes, then check the level again.

evidence.title: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide
evidence.section: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide › 4 Faults

segments.text: A fault stops the motor and shows its code on the display.
Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F004 | Earth fault | Damaged motor cable or wet motor | Measure the insulation before resetting |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F010 | Analog input lost | Speed reference below 2 mA on a 4 to 20 mA input | Check the reference cable and its source |
| F011 | Output short circuit | Short circuit in the motor cable or motor | Disconnect and test the motor cable |
| F013 | Motor stall | Motor below 5 percent of set speed at full current | Free the jammed load |
| F015 | Parameter memory error | Corrupt parameters after a power cut during a save | Restore the parameter backup |
| F016 | Cooling fan failure | Fan blocked or worn out | Replace fan PN-7716-A |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
## Fault F012: output overcurrent
Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating.
The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.
A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds.
Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.
## Fault F002: DC bus overvoltage
Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V.
It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load.
## Fault F010: analog input lost
Fault F010 means the speed reference on a 4 to 20 mA input fell below 2 mA, which the drive reads as a broken wire.
The drive stops the motor rather than run at an unknown speed.

segments.text: # Safety bulletin SB-0947: Hot work permits
Welding, grinding and cutting outside the workshops need a hot work permit from the shift supervisor.
Remove or cover combustible material within 10 meters, keep a fire extinguisher at the work site and post a fire watch for 60 minutes after the work ends.
Hot work on a line that has carried oil or solvent also needs a gas test before the permit is signed.
The permit is valid for one shift.
If the work isn't finished by the end of the shift, the next shift supervisor issues a new permit after checking the site again.

segments.text: # Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.
Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing.
Verify zero energy before work starts.
Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.
At the Riverside plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Riverside maintenance planner on extension 4410 before work starts.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 1 Safety

segments.text: # 1 Safety
Read this manual before installing, operating or servicing the pump.
Work on the pump only when you are trained for the task and the pump is isolated as your site's procedures require.
- Isolate the motor electrically and lock it out before any work on the pump.
- Release the pressure in the casing and the seal-water line before opening any connection.
- Wear safety glasses and gloves when handling the mechanical seal.
The seal faces are brittle and their edges are sharp.
- Never run the pump dry or against a closed suction valve.
- Lift the pump only by the lifting lugs on the baseplate, never by the motor eyebolt.
# 2 Description
The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C.
The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.
The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply.
Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft.
A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

segments.text: # Procurement policy PROC-POL-007: Purchase approvals
Every purchase order needs an approver other than the requester.
Orders above 25,000 USD need a second approval from the plant controller, and orders above 250,000 USD need the CFO's approval.
Buy only from qualified suppliers.
A new supplier is qualified after a quality audit and a credit check, and Procurement re-qualifies each supplier every three years.
Approval limits
| Order value | Approvals needed |
| Up to 25,000 USD | One approver other than the requester |
| 25,000 to 250,000 USD | The approver and the plant controller |
| Above 250,000 USD | The approver, the plant controller and the CFO |
Splitting an order to stay under an approval limit is a breach of this policy.
Emergency orders outside working hours may be placed by the duty manager and approved on the next business day.

evidence.title: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
evidence.section: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

segments.text: # Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.
Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing.
Verify zero energy before work starts.
Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open.
Each person working on the pump fits their own lock.

evidence.title: HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027
evidence.section: HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027

segments.text: # HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027
This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027.
From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.
The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged.
Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy.
Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.
## Questions managers may hear
Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started.
They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.
Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.

segments.text: ## Error E-103: wrong phase sequence
Error E-103 means the supply phase sequence is reversed, so the pump would run backwards.
The controller blocks the start; it never trips a running pump for E-103.
Causes, most likely first:
1. Two supply cables were swapped during electrical work.

evidence.section: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide › 4 Faults

segments.text: # 4 Faults
Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.
Table 4-1 Fault codes
| Code | Fault | Likely cause | Remedy |
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F002 | DC bus overvoltage | Ramp-down time too short for the load's inertia | Raise parameter 2-11 or fit a brake resistor |
| F003 | Heatsink overtemperature | Blocked air flow or a failed fan | Clean the air path; check the fan (F016) |
| F004 | Earth fault | Damaged motor cable or wet motor | Measure the insulation before resetting |
| F005 | Motor overload (I²t) | Motor current above its rating for too long | Check the load; check parameter 1-03 |
| F006 | Input phase loss | A blown supply fuse | Replace the fuse and find out why it blew |
| F007 | Motor phase loss | Loose motor cable terminal | Tighten the motor terminals |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
